_README: This is a TASTE SPECIFICATION. A person uses it to record what they find good about generated designs, expressed ONLY in terms of properties that can be measured with no observer — physical facts, not opinions. An automated system reads this file as a starting belief (a 'prior') about the person's taste, then refines it from the person's actual A-vs-B choices over time. It exists so the system can rank options the way this person would without interrupting them for every decision. Nothing in here is decided by an AI: an AI may help you DRAFT it, but only the human commits it, and the system never substitutes an AI's opinion of what is good for the human's.
_GOVERNANCE: HUMAN-ONLY. Copy this file to taste.json and edit it to your taste. An AI may PROPOSE edits (staged for your approval) but MUST NEVER write taste.json. Only you commit taste. This is your reference; the machine only attunes to it.

_fields.weight: How much this property pulls the preference, and which way. Positive = more of it is preferred; negative = less is preferred; 0 = it does not affect the preference at all. Magnitude = strength: a weight of 2 pulls twice as hard as 1. Weights are on a standardized scale (see 'scale'), so a weight means the same thing across different properties and they are directly comparable.
_fields.conviction: How firmly the weight is held — how much contrary evidence it takes to move it. Higher = more stubborn. As a rule of thumb, each recorded A-vs-B choice adds about 0.25 of evidence, so a conviction of 5 resists on the order of 20 contrary choices before it bends. Use high conviction for tastes you are sure of, low for hunches you want the data to shape. (Conviction only matters once 'weight' is non-zero.)
_fields.scale: The characteristic spread of this property across real designs — the size of a 'normal' difference in it. It exists solely to put every property on one comparable footing so 'weight' is meaningful everywhere. Set it near the property's real range. It is a fact about the property, not a taste.

_what_the_axes_are: Each entry under 'axes' is ONE measurable property of a design — something a system computes by observing the design, with no human judgment involved. Taste is expressed as weights OVER these facts; the facts themselves are never opinions. You may add, remove, or replace axes freely, but every axis MUST be something measurable with no observer. If a proposed axis could only be settled by someone's judgment, it does not belong here — the judgment belongs in the weights, or nowhere. (The four axes below come from one specific feature; a different feature would declare its own. They are shown so the shape is concrete.)
_how_to_use_this: To express what you value, set each axis's weight (sign = direction, size = strength) and conviction (how sure you are); leave 'scale' near the property's real spread. Start from the zero weights below — a blank slate expressing no taste yet — and add only what you can defend. NOTE: while every weight is 0, the system has nothing to rank by and will ask you about each choice; the moment you set weights, it begins deciding for you within them. You are the only writer of the committed file.

_illustration._note: A worked example of the MECHANICS ONLY. It expresses no taste you should adopt — it just shows how the three numbers read together.
_illustration._reads_as: This person moderately prefers designs with MORE of 'some_property' (positive weight 1.5), is fairly sure of it (conviction 3 — it would take roughly a dozen contrary choices to soften), and a normal difference in this property is about 10 units (scale 10), which is what makes the weight of 1.5 comparable to weights on other properties.

skill_gap._measures: How much better a skilled attempt does than a random one — the room there is to be good. 1 means skill buys nothing (the outcome is luck); higher means more room for mastery.

punishes_naive._measures: How much the obvious-but-wrong strategy costs compared with doing nothing. 1 means the naive approach is harmless; above 1 means it actively backfires — there is a trap to learn to avoid.

learnability._measures: How much an attempt improves by paying attention and adjusting, rather than staying flat. 0 means attention does not help; toward 1 means practice pays off strongly.

headroom._measures: Where the best achievable attempt lands relative to trivial. Near 0 means the best is basically handed to you (too easy); near 1 means even the best barely makes a dent (too hard). It measures how much is left on the table at mastery.
